Austin is called a "naive empiricist" most plausibly because his account of law rests on an anachronistic model of a legal system. He reads law off observable facts: a determinate sovereign, commands backed by sanctions, and a habit of obedience. That picture fits a centralised modern state, so it fits poorly with customary, diffuse or constitutionally limited legal orders. I'm choosing this over "he denies any link between law and morality" because that claim oversimplifies Austin, who tied law to utilitarian morality. I'm picking between the two options you gave and can't confirm the source.

CONFIDENCE: 55
